title: Ion Pumps and Metal Toxicity
topicTitle: Ion pumps (sodium-potassium and sodium-glucose pump); metal toxicity (iron, arsenic, mercury, lead and cadmium)
notes: **$Na^+/K^+$ pump:** maintains high K$^+$ and low Na$^+$ inside cells. Essential for nerve impulse transmission, muscle contraction, and cell volume regulation. Consumes about 25% of resting ATP in humans.
**Sodium-glucose cotransporter (SGLT):** couples downhill Na movement to uphill glucose transport. Found in intestinal epithelium and renal tubules.
**Iron toxicity:** iron catalyses Fenton reaction: $Fe^{2+} + H_2O_2 \rightarrow Fe^{3+} + OH^- + \cdot OH$. Hydroxyl radical damages DNA, proteins and lipids.
**Arsenic toxicity:** $As^{3+}$ binds to vicinal dithiols in enzymes like pyruvate dehydrogenase, blocking cellular respiration.
**Mercury toxicity:** $Hg^{2+}$ has high affinity for $-SH$ groups. Binds to cysteine residues, denaturing enzymes. Minamata disease was mercury poisoning from industrial discharge.
**Lead toxicity:** $Pb^{2+}$ mimics Ca$^{2+}$ and disrupts neurotransmitter release, bone formation, and haem synthesis. Causes anaemia and neurological damage.
**Cadmium toxicity:** accumulates in kidneys, replaces Zn in enzymes, causing renal dysfunction and itai-itai disease.
